newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates rise as funds leave for stocks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates rise as funds leave for stocks.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates rose at mid-session on Wednesday amid active exodus of funds out of the banking system into the red hot stock market, dealers said.

At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 7.137 percent against Tuesday's 6.856 finish -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still far below the double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper rose to 7.50-7.75 percent against 7.00-7.50.
The stock market on Wednesday closed 0.62 percent or 57.41 points higher to reach a seven-year peak of 9,362.68.
Dealers said they expected the rates to continue rising if the central bank opted not to inject funds to loosen liquidity.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9775-9800 percent against 5.9250.
